answer: At dusk the wage book is opened, and every picker is paid for the baskets he carried, signing beside his name. A harbor picker who never worked fails the book: the baskets must be the picker's own, counted at the ember of the press, and a name with no baskets earns nothing at all. Buying a false wage book costs a forger 6,800 in bribes to the paymaster and fees to the pickers, while the opal entry in the book is checked at every payday, so a picker whose baskets were never counted is turned away.
